a: ACT SECOND - The revenge of a savage
t: Scene: Lima, and other districts of Peru
d: Wide plain, watered by the Rima: the east is full of majestic clouds, burdened by the rays of the rising sun. Otumbo, at the head of a tribe of Americans, dragging Alvaro among chains.
Piazza di Lima. To the happy sound of war instruments deployed the Spanish militias: the officers gather in crocchio.
Alvaro, Gusmano, Ataliba, other offices, and sayings.
Apartment intended for Ataliba, in the palace of the Governor. Zuma moves silently, followed by other American ladies. Alzira.
Gusman, Atalibah, and sayings, then Officers, and Spanish Soldiers, Zuma, and American Donzelle.

Internal part of the fortifications of Lima. Here and there Spanish drapples, which drink cheerfully: meanwhile, some American prisoners, among which Zamoro, cross the scene at the bottom, loaded with stumps, and among soldiers who guard them.

Orrid cave, just illuminated by moon anage, which descends there across a foram. The scene remains empty some time, then Otumbo looks, and beats to a golden shield, hanging suspended; then a remnant of the defeated Americans pops up from the most sinuous parts of the cave, where it was appiated.

Zamorus, and sayings. He wears the clothes of a Spanish soldier. Upon his arrival they all bow down; it raises them up with a nod; then slowly turns his eyes, full of dark sadness, and casts a look, as shame, at the spoils of which it is covered. Silence.

Large Hall in the Governor's residence, with loggias in the bottom, from which I glimpsed the illuminated city: in the middle a gallery, to which one ascends for three or four steps. The loco is all emblazoned by Spanish militias: the dukes stand on the gallery, the handmaids of Alzira on one song: they echo gladly.
Gusmano, Alzira, Alvaro, Ataliba, Ovando, Zuma, and sayings.
